why: Washington County's Ordinance ORD-2026-12 imposes a countywide moratorium on data center applications effective June 30, 2026, for a period of six months (computed expiration December 29, 2026), deferring acceptance and approval of all such applications, and the site is within the county scope. The project has not submitted permits, and the exemption for existing Certificate of Use & Occupancy does not apply to new data centers. The project's 300 MW load assumes an N+1 backup design of 121 diesel generators at 2,500 kW each, yielding an estimated NOx potential to emit of 1,067 tpy, which exceeds the 100 tpy major-source threshold under 40 CFR 70.2 and triggers a federal Title V operating permit requirement. The Title V major-source determination rests on assumptions of 500 hours/year emergency-engine PTE and 6.4 g/kWh NOx (Tier 2 diesel) that have not been verified for this project. Because the county moratorium creates an immediate barrier to any data center application processing, and the federal air permit requirement adds a major, assumption-dependent layer, the project cannot proceed under current conditions.
